topic: For fixed binary potential outcomes and uniform assignment of exactly half of a positive even population to treatment, let rho_n^CR be worst-schedule squared-error minimax risk for ATE estimators using both arm-success counts and let rho_n^W restrict rules to W=2(X_1-X_0). Prove rho_n^CR=rho_n^W at n=2,4,6 and rho_8^CR<rho_8^W. Supply analytic primal/least-favorable-prior equality certificates, including the algebraic seven-state n=6 saddle, and a serialized rational n=8 two-count upper certificate and W-only prior lower certificate proving rho_8^CR<0.06541<0.06578<rho_8^W. Derive the exact response-type hypergeometric games and explain why the second count first changes the minimax envelope at eight. Treat later-even persistence and every higher-order balance-tax law as open; make no confidence-set or pointwise-dominance claim. The consumer is DeclareDesign randomizr::complete_ra, whose exact-balance users learn the first small-n setting where reducing two counts to their difference is minimax-lossy. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Fresh exact checks verify rho_2=1/4, rho_4=1-sqrt(3)/2, an algebraic seven-state equality saddle at n=6, and the rational n=8 sandwich 457801172643/7000000000000<0.06541<0.06578<224641744872980943629642927781/3414537001722982784239360000000. A strengthened standard-library verifier checks legal assignments, positive priors, radical isolation, active-risk identities, every full-count posterior equation, inactive constraints, and certificate directions. Bounded searches found no exact-cutoff collision; Hull v3 leaves the related complete-randomization question conjectural. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently reconstruct the four finite certificates directly from the response-type hypergeometric kernel, separately from the embedded labeled-assignment enumerator. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the n=6 seven-state saddle from hypergeometric coefficients and verify every posterior identity and all 77 inactive inequalities exactly; any mismatch stops the finite headline. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_complete_balance_secondorder.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Independently determine whether the full arm-success pair and its difference have equal ATE squared-error minimax risk at n=2,4,6 but first separate strictly at n=8 under balanced complete randomization.

source_refs.claim: Hull optimizes over general estimators globally but leaves the corresponding complete-randomization problem conjectural after numerical investigation.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: The unrestricted binary-outcome minimax game is solved, while complete randomization is evaluated using difference-in-means rather than its optimal unrestricted rule.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Binary completely randomized experiments admit an exact representation through an observed 2x2 table and a latent four-response-type table.
source_refs.author: Peng Ding, Tirthankar Dasgupta
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: The scalar reduction used for unrestricted Bernoulli assignment relies on a shifted-binomial experiment, whereas conditioning on exactly n/2 treated units produces a response-type multivariate-hypergeometric likelihood depending on both observed counts. Existing complete-randomization comparisons generally optimize a prescribed affine or difference-in-means estimator, so they cannot determine the unrestricted minimax value of the discarded total-success coordinate. The supplied presolve certificates remain hypotheses until the four finite games, especially the seven-state n=6 saddle and all inactive inequalities, are reconstructed directly from the hypergeometric kernel.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact finite-game characterization giving matching estimator and least-favorable-prior certificates at n=2,4,6 and rational full-count upper and W-only prior lower certificates proving strict separation at n=8.

writing_exemplar.why: Its reversal narrative motivates auditing familiar balancing prescriptions once bounded outcomes permit nonlinear minimax estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: complete randomization is conventionally efficiency-improving -> bounded outcomes make additional assignment information decision-relevant -> unrestricted nonlinear estimation changes minimax comparisons -> locate the first size where the second count has minimax value

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce binary schedules by permutation orbits, formulate the resulting finite convex minimax game, and certify a posterior-mean estimator using a least-favorable prior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required certificates are the fixed-complete-randomization analogues of its estimator-prior saddles, with hypergeometric rather than shifted-binomial likelihoods.

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize the potential-outcome schedule by four binary response-type counts and derive the exact randomization law of the observed table.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those response-type counts and table probabilities provide the exact state-observation kernel needed for an independent certificate reconstruction.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the even sample sizes for which the full arm-success pair and W=2(X1-X0) have equal minimax value, and decide whether the strict full-data advantage persists for every even n at least 8.

source_refs.claim: Hull reports numerical strict suboptimality for complete randomization at moderate sizes and leaves its general persistence conjectural.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: Blackwell characterizes finite-experiment garbling, which yields weak dominance of full counts over their deterministic compression but not strictness for this loss.
source_refs.author: David Blackwell

source_refs.excerpt: For K=2 and c=(1,-1), all four response-type counts remain in the orbit likelihood.
preserve the full four-type orbit experiment ... do not claim that effect-class aggregation itself identifies the likeli

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior orbit theorem deliberately retains all four response-type counts and does not establish likelihood sufficiency of an effect-class statistic. Blackwell garbling proves only the weak inequality because W is a deterministic function of the pair. Strictness does not automatically propagate from n to n+2: fixed-half sampling changes the feasible response-type lattice, parity constraints, hypergeometric likelihoods, and potentially the least-favorable support. A persistence result therefore needs a uniform separating-prior construction or a valid lifting argument across successive even population sizes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A classification theorem giving the exact equality set in even n and, on every strict branch, explicit full-count primal and W-only least-favorable-prior certificates with a positive risk-gap formula or certified lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from an exact finite game to structural conclusions is the right model for turning a small-n phase change into a persistence question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: binary finite-population minimaxity reduces to a finite decision game -> nonlinear least-favorable behavior appears beyond standard estimators -> small-n analysis reveals a phase change -> determine whether that phase persists along every later even size

method_exemplars.technique: Represent compression as a Markov kernel and use posterior-risk geometry or a separating decision problem to detect strict value of information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The full-count experiment deterministically garbles to W, so the missing step is showing that the garbling remains consequential for the ATE squared-loss game at every later size.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite minimax duality, orbit reduction, posterior-mean rules, and least-favorable priors to produce matched upper and lower risk witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A persistence proof needs the same estimator-prior duality, augmented by an induction or stability argument for without-replacement two-count likelihoods.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the asymptotic balance-compression tax Delta_n=rho_n^W-rho_n^CR, including its first nonzero normalization, leading constant or subsequential-limit set, and whether it is smaller-order than the common n^{-4/3} improvement.

source_refs.claim: For the unrestricted binary game, the minimax risk has an n^{-1}-C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}) expansion derived from a discrete Stein identity and Airy variational problem.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Finite-population central limit theorems control first-order randomization asymptotics but do not determine higher-order minimax information loss from statistic compression.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: They further prove rho_n(c)=n^{-1}-C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}), with C_A=1.617...
Whether any regularly varying normalization has a finite positive second-order limit is open

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available Airy calculation uses independent Rademacher noise and a scalar reduced observation. Exact-half assignment instead generates a negatively dependent bivariate hypergeometric experiment, while the W restriction projects away the total-success coordinate. Neither the scalar Stein identity nor its boundary-variance expansion transfers unchanged, and ordinary finite-population CLTs do not identify the finer decision-theoretic value of the omitted coordinate. The first proof step requiring replacement is therefore the local likelihood and Stein expansion, which must retain both coordinates before comparing it with its projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem identifying a normalization a_n and positive limit L, or the complete subsequential-limit set, for a_n(rho_n^W-rho_n^CR), with matched full-count estimator upper bounds and W-only least-favorable-prior lower bounds at that scale.

writing_exemplar.why: Its first-order-benchmark to nonstandard second-order-correction narrative directly fits a higher-order loss caused by balance and compression.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: balanced randomization gives a first-order minimax benchmark -> nonlinear shrinkage yields an n^{-4/3} correction -> a least-favorable boundary layer determines the sharp constant -> quantify the finer tax from compressing the exact-balance experiment

method_exemplars.technique: Perturb the unbiased rule at the boundary scale, expand risk with a discrete Stein identity, solve the induced variational problem, and discretize the ground-state density into a least-favorable prior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is another second-order minimax expansion, but its first analytic layer must be rebuilt for a conditional hypergeometric pair and its one-dimensional projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate without-replacement randomization statistics through finite-population central limit arguments under explicit maximal-term conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its normalization and coupling machinery provide the first approximation layer before the sharper boundary correction needed to separate full counts from W.

open_problems.open_problem: Give necessary and sufficient conditions on a two-arm assignment law and statistic T(X1,X0), specializing to T=W, for T to preserve the full binary finite-population ATE minimax value.

source_refs.excerpt: The orbit equality also does not rule out some other scalar representation.
state a necessary-and-sufficient condition for any scalar ancillary reduction, or an explicit generic obstruction
It proves scalar Bayes-risk equivalence for a chosen prior but asserts neither least-favorability nor equality

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing arguments establish scalar Bayes-risk equivalence for selected priors or import minimax equality from a separate value theorem; neither supplies an experiment-level criterion uniform over the priors relevant to minimaxity. Under fixed-half assignment, conditioning on W leaves several full-count cells whose posterior ATE means may differ. A valid characterization must therefore distinguish ordinary likelihood sufficiency, prior-specific Rao-Blackwell equivalence, Blackwell equivalence, and equality only for the particular ATE squared-loss game.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if theorem stated through response-type likelihood matrices or Blackwell kernels, characterizing when every full-data minimax rule has a T-measurable risk-equivalent rule and providing a finite separating-prior certificate whenever the condition fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats scalar reduction as a substantive minimax result rather than merely an implementation convenience.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: the labeled response experiment is large -> a scalar transformation can preserve posterior risk under special structure -> scalarization unlocks an exact saddle -> characterize precisely which assignment-statistic pairs admit that reduction

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize comparison of finite experiments through stochastic kernels and use separating decision rules when no reverse kernel exists.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is an ATE-specific refinement of experiment comparison, separating universal Blackwell sufficiency from minimax-value preservation for one target and loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine prior-specific Rao-Blackwellization with finite minimax duality to show that a scalar posterior mean attains a full-game value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof supplies the positive model case; the characterization must isolate the exact conditional-kernel identity that makes the reduction valid.

open_problems.open_problem: For every fixed treatment count m in an n-unit binary completely randomized experiment, classify when the full arm-success pair has lower minimax ATE risk than the natural difference-in-arm-means contrast and determine which m minimizes each risk.

source_refs.claim: Bai jointly studies complete randomization, linear estimation, and the treatment count through Neyman allocation under permutation-invariant outcome classes.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

source_refs.claim: For bounded potential outcomes and arbitrary estimators, realized treatment-share variation can carry information unavailable under a fixed-share design.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: The binary complete-randomization response-type formulation permits general treated and control counts and exact observed-table likelihoods.
source_refs.author: Peng Ding, Tirthankar Dasgupta
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing allocation results are tied to linear difference-in-means-type estimators or outcome classes that do not exploit binary boundedness through nonlinear shrinkage. Moving away from m=n/2 destroys the treatment-control involution used in the balanced game, changes the feasible count rectangle, and yields asymmetric multivariate-hypergeometric coefficients. Searches locate exact confidence procedures for general m and minimax designs for prescribed estimators, but not an arbitrary-estimator risk map comparing the full count pair with its scalar contrast.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite theorem characterizing rho_{n,m}^{full} and rho_{n,m}^{contrast}, their equality and strictness regions over 1≤m≤n-1, and the exact or asymptotic minimizers of each risk over m.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents the treated count as a design choice rather than a fixed convention, which is the natural framing for the destination problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: permutation symmetry supports complete randomization -> precision depends on the treatment count -> classical minimax allocation is derived under linear formulations -> binary bounded schedules require an exact nonlinear allocation-and-compression map

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize a finite quadratic-risk game over arbitrary estimators and certify its solution with a posterior mean under a least-favorable prior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same bounded-support saddle machinery applies after replacing the balanced kernel by its asymmetric fixed-m counterpart.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the four-response-type table and the general treated-control randomization distribution to enumerate compatible observations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This provides the exact likelihood kernel needed to define both finite minimax games at every allocation.

open_problems.open_problem: For K≥3 binary arms under a fixed exact allocation vector, characterize when the full vector of arm-success counts is minimax-equivalent to a scalar contrast score and determine the first population size and allocation where compression is strictly lossy.

source_refs.excerpt: the map from the full data to (Z_i) is not minimax-preserving, even at the fixed q-star design
add a standalone strict K=3-versus-K=2 nonreducibility theorem tying the eight-type likelihood

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior construction supplies a finite K=3 information-loss witness under an independent fixed-q design, but exact allocation replaces its product likelihood by a multivariate-hypergeometric response-type kernel. Consequently neither the witness nor its ancillary obstruction transfers verbatim. The first proof step that changes is the allocation-count likelihood and its orbit stabilizer; one must determine whether fixed margins erase, preserve, or amplify transverse arm-label information before making any threshold claim.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fixed-allocation nonreducibility theorem giving a likelihood-matrix criterion and an explicit smallest-(n,r) primal-dual saddle pair that strictly separates the full success-count vector from every scalar-contrast-measurable rule.

writing_exemplar.why: Its finite-population treatment of multi-arm contrasts and unequal replication provides the appropriate destination-language.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: complex experiments use multiple treatment arms -> finite-population contrasts encode scientific comparisons -> exact allocation determines their randomization law -> decide whether the scalar contrast discards minimax-relevant arm-count information

method_exemplars.technique: Construct posterior-mean minimax rules and least-favorable-prior certificates after response-schedule orbit reduction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the scalar two-arm benchmark whose ancillary mechanism must either generalize to the K-arm hypergeometric kernel or be defeated by a separating prior.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize exactly balanced assignment designs through minimax risk and assignment second-moment geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its exact-allocation design architecture is the closest available framework for comparing full-data and scalar-analysis minimax values across several arms.

literature_map:
Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, arXiv:2608.13822) solve the unrestricted binary design-estimator game through a shifted-binomial reduction, nonlinear shrinkage, least-favorable priors, and an Airy n^-4/3 correction.
Hull (2026, arXiv:2608.09812) independently analyzes bounded-outcome minimax design and explicitly leaves general-estimator complete-randomization strictness conjectural.
Hull also identifies affine penalties from balanced and paired assignment, exposing a broader balance-versus-information tension.
Ding and Dasgupta (2016, JASA, arXiv:1501.02389) supply the four-response-type and observed-2x2-table representation needed for exact binary complete-randomization kernels.
Rigdon and Hudgens (2015, Statistics in Medicine, DOI 10.1002/sim.6384) develop finite-sample randomization inference for the binary-outcome ATE.
Li and Ding (2016, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv:1509.07138) use hypergeometric stochastic order to accelerate exact binary-outcome procedures.
Zhang et al. (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2305.09906) sharpen balanced-design exact computation, confirming that exact balance materially changes observed-table combinatorics.
Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1405.6555) derive sharp finite-population variance bounds for difference-in-means rather than unrestricted minimax point estimation.
Li and Ding (2017, JASA, arXiv:1610.04821) provide finite-population CLT tools for without-replacement randomization but not higher-order compression risk.
Kallus (2018, JRSSB, arXiv:1312.0531) and Kallus (2021, JRSSB, arXiv:2005.03151) develop minimax design arguments under variance criteria and emphasize balance-robustness tradeoffs.
Bai (2023, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.10.009) studies complete randomization and treatment-count choice under permutation invariance, with estimator optimization restricted to a linear class.
Bai (2022, AER, arXiv:2206.07845) proves matched-pair precision optimality under prognostic matching, creating tension with worst-schedule penalties from repeated exact balance.
Harshaw, Savje, Spielman, and Zhang (2024, JASA, arXiv:1911.03071) formalize a balance-versus-worst-case-MSE robustness frontier.
Aronow and Lopatto (2026, arXiv:2605.20572) provide an adjacent minimax certificate template for unbiased bounded-total procedures.
Blackwell (1953, Annals of Mathematical Statistics, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177729032) implies weak dominance of full counts over their compression, while strict value for ATE squared loss requires an additional witness.
prior_proposal_map:
The closest source is accepted qid exp_multiarm_secondorder_minimax_frontier/v1: its proto_core and writeup retain the full four-response-type K=2 orbit likelihood and explicitly disclaim likelihood-level scalar reduction.
Its reviewers repeatedly requested necessary-and-sufficient scalar nonreducibility criteria and exact small-n primal-dual exhibits; angle0_v1 and angle0_v4 were the highest-yield JSONs.
The same accepted run supplies the adjacent n^-4/3 Airy benchmark, rational orbit-game machinery, and the warning that same-n certificates do not establish cross-n limits.
Failed qid exp_multiarm_sharp_secondorder_limit/v1 was inspected for abandoned nonreducibility and finite-to-limit directions; angle0_v4 requests an eight-type transverse obstruction.
Downgraded qid exp_prognostic_design_admissibility/v1 was inspected as the nearest exact-balance design entry; it studies a fixed difference-in-means estimator and does not duplicate unrestricted full-count-versus-W minimaxity.
Its README and review_general warn against inferring global dominance from an n=8 witness, reinforcing the need for explicit all-n certificates.
No relevant archived rejected-angle proposal was found among the adjacent complete-randomization/minimax qids, and the current qid had no proposal artifact to mine.
